additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body weight and shape, but individuals are typically of normal weight or overweight, distinguishing it from classic presentations of anorexia nervosa. The course is often fluctuating, with periods of more frequent episodes during times of stress, transitions, or weight-focused environments, and it commonly co-occurs with mood and anxiety symptoms. Clinically, it is differentiated from binge-eating disorder by the presence of compensatory behaviors and from non-pathological overeating by the recurrent, intrusive nature of the behaviors and associated distress and impairment.

patient.stressor: Daphne’s difficulties around food became more intense after she returned from a trip to Kyoto about a year ago, where she was struck by how slim and put-together many people looked compared to how she saw herself in photos from the trip. Back home in Okanogan County, she threw herself into eco-fashion projects and online art communities, many of which emphasized minimalism and "clean eating" aesthetics that made her increasingly critical of her own body when she compared it to stylized images of other textile artists. During a particularly stressful period at the shop—juggling a rush of wedding garments, vendor disputes, and late-night dye experiments—she began coping by eating large, improvised meals alone in her small kitchen after work, then feeling panicked about the impact on her body and taking drastic measures to counteract it. Over six months, this cycle escalated, she withdrew from hikes and yoga classes out of embarrassment about how she looked, and a close friend from her local art center finally urged her to seek psychiatric help after Daphne confided that her eating and efforts to control her weight felt "out of control" and were crowding out her art and sleep.
patient.chief_complaint: “Once I start eating in the evenings, it feels like I can’t stop or control it at all.”

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If the scale is even a pound higher or I see the slightest bulge in a photo, I panic and start thinking, ‘I’m going to blow up and look huge in my clothes,’ and it feels like my whole day is ruined until I do something to get the weight back down.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Most days I decide if I’m worth anything by how flat my stomach looks in the mirror before my shower, and if I see any roll or softness I just feel like a failure, no matter how well I did at work or with my art projects.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a bad binge, I’ll force myself to go for long, punishing walks up and down the hills after my shift and then skip meals the next day, telling myself I don’t deserve to eat until I’ve made up for what I did.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: Lately, when I eat too much at night, I end up in the bathroom making myself throw up until my throat burns, or I’ll take a handful of laxatives before bed because I can’t stand the thought of all that food staying in me.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On those nights after the shop, I can stand at my tiny kitchen counter and go through half a loaf of bread with peanut butter, a frozen pizza, leftover takeout, and whatever snacks are around in less than an hour, even when I wasn’t that hungry to start with.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start in on the evening eating, it’s like a switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in, telling myself to stop while my hands keep going back to the fridge or the cupboards until I feel sick and ashamed.
